note: three of the four findings are defects I introduced WHILE fixing the previous ones: the streams were confined and the metadata about them was not

confirmed: _status read capture-status.json with an ordinary open, so a symlink supplied ANOTHER attempt's word and a prefix log was reported as captured
record_capture opened .staging with an ordinary truncating open, so a symlink there made it OVERWRITE the file it pointed at -- an actual write outside the attempt's room
R1_sidecar_escaped_the_boundary.correction: metadata obeys the stream rules: opened relative to the held room, no-follow, regular-file, bounded read; staging created O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW; the replace anchored to that descriptor at both ends; on failure the staging entry is removed and the stream's own log is untouched
cases: a status symlink does not supply another attempt's word
a staging symlink does not overwrite what it points at, and the sibling still says what it said
a status that is a special file is corrupt, not a blocked read

R2_atomic_replacement_is_not_an_atomic_u.confirmed: record_capture loaded one shared document, changed one entry and replaced the whole thing; a second writer recording stderr=failed while the first was mid-update had its failure vanish
R2_atomic_replacement_is_not_an_atomic_u.correction: ONE SIDECAR PER STREAM rather than a lock. No two writers touch one file, because a stream is written by the one thing that writes that stream, and the staging name is per-stream so overlapping writes cannot collide
cases: two streams declared concurrently both survive
declaring one stream leaves the others alone

R3_corrupt_metadata_must_not_take_down_t.confirmed: a valid JSON object whose entry was the integer 1 crashed locators with a TypeError
R3_corrupt_metadata_must_not_take_down_t.correction: every member checked -- shape, declared state, bounded reason, bounded document. Anything else is `corrupt`: REPORTED, never raised, and never silently turned into an assertion of completeness. The raw log stays readable and the other streams still answer. Every result carries a `declaration` field so 'no writer's word' and 'the writer said nothing' are distinguishable.
cases: nine malformed shapes: integer, list, string, non-JSON, non-UTF-8, invented state, missing reason, non-text reason, oversized document
the whole operator view still answers with corrupt metadata, and the raw log is still readable

two_expectations_I_got_wrong: I asserted an oversized reason is REFUSED; it is truncated, as every other bounded diagnostic in this package is, with MAX_STATUS as the document backstop. Corrected the case, not the code.

a fixture declared `partial` for a stream with no file and expected `partial` back; `partial` says what is HERE is a prefix, so with nothing there `absent` is the honest answer. The fixture writes the log first.
